questions.question: 96 + 58 - 63 + (35 + 17) times 2 - 89 = ?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Solve the bracket and multiplication first: (35 + 17) × 2 = 52 × 2 = 104.

Group positive and negative terms: (96 + 58 + 104) − (63 + 89).

Total Positives = 258 | Total Negatives = 152.

Final Result = 258 − 152 = 106.

**∴ The correct answer is 106.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 96 + 58 − 63 + (35 + 17) × 2 − 89

**Formula:** Apply BODMAS Rule (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

⇒ 96 + 58 − 63 + (52) × 2 − 89

⇒ 96 + 58 − 63 + 104 − 89

⇒ 154 − 63 + 104 − 89

⇒ 91 + 104 − 89

⇒ 195 − 89

⇒ 106

**∴ The correct answer is 106.**

**__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It defines the order of operations: Brackets (), Orders (powers/roots), Division (÷), Multiplication (×), Addition (+), and Subtraction (−).

Grouping Technique

To avoid errors in long addition/subtraction strings, sum all positive numbers and all negative numbers separately, then find their difference.

Multiplication Priority

Always complete multiplication operations following brackets before moving to addition or subtraction to ensure calculation accuracy.

questions.question: 72 + 28 - (22 div 2) + 33 times 1 + 19 { of } 1 - 16 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the operations in order: (Bracket), (Of), (Division), (Multiplication), (Addition/Subtraction).

Evaluate terms: (22 ÷ 2) = 11, 33 × 1 = 33, and 19 of 1 = 19.

The expression becomes: 72 + 28 − 11 + 33 + 19 − 16.

Group positive and negative terms: (72 + 28 + 33 + 19) − (11 + 16) = 152 − 27 = 125.

**∴ The correct answer is 125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 72 + 28 − (22 ÷ 2) + 33 × 1 + 19 of 1 − 16

**Formula Used:** BODMAS Rule (Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

⇒ 72 + 28 − 11 + 33 × 1 + 19 of 1 − 16 (Solving Bracket)

⇒ 72 + 28 − 11 + 33 × 1 + 19 − 16 (Solving 'Of' → 19 × 1)

⇒ 72 + 28 − 11 + 33 + 19 − 16 (Solving Multiplication → 33 × 1)

⇒ 100 − 11 + 33 + 19 − 16 (Addition from left)

⇒ 89 + 33 + 19 − 16

⇒ 122 + 19 − 16

⇒ 141 − 16

⇒ 125

**∴ The correct answer is 125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It defines the sequence of operations: Brackets (), Of (Orders/powers), Division (÷), Multiplication (×), Addition (+), and Subtraction (−).

Priority of 'Of'

The 'Of' operation is essentially multiplication but must be performed before division and after brackets.

Left-to-Right Rule

When operations of the same priority level (like Addition and Subtraction or Multiplication and Division) appear, they are solved from left to right.

questions.question: The ratio of two numbers is 3:2, and their product is 726. Find the larger number and also find the difference between the two numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Product of ratio parts = 3 × 2 = 6 units².

Given product = 726 ⇒ 6 units² = 726.

1 unit² = 726 ÷ 6 = 121 ⇒ 1 unit = √121 = 11.

Larger number = 3 units = 3 × 11 = 33.

Difference = (3 − 2) units = 1 unit = 11.

**∴ The correct answer is 33, 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Ratio of numbers = 3 : 2, Product = 726.

Formula: Let the numbers be 3x and 2x.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2d0fc139d72ff04cbc51849ca8b0743dbd6fe1e4d686e5dd02445a12a30d4c6e.png] 

⇒ (3x) × (2x) = 726

⇒ 6x² = 726

⇒ x² = 726 ÷ 6

⇒ x² = 121

⇒ x = √121 = 11

⇒ Larger number = 3x = 3 × 11 = 33

⇒ Smaller number = 2x = 2 × 11 = 22

⇒ Difference = 33 − 22 = 11

**∴ The correct answer is 33, 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Multiplier Property

When two numbers are in ratio a:b, they can be represented as ax and bx, where x is the highest common factor (HCF).

Product of Ratios

If the product of two numbers is P and the ratio is a:b, then x = √(P ÷ (a × b)).

Duplicate Ratio

The duplicate ratio of a:b is a² : b², which often appears in problems involving areas or products.

questions.question: A chord of length 20 cm makes an angle of 90° at the center of a circle. Find the radius of the circle and the distance of this chord from the center.

⇒ Radius (r) = 20 / √2 = 10√2 cm.

⇒ Distance (d) = 20 / 2 = 10 cm.

Mixed Fractions

questions.question: Which of the following options will have sum as (7/8)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the sum 7/8, convert all fractions to have a common denominator of 8.

Option 1: 1/8 + 4/8 = 5/8

Option 2: 4/8 + 3/8 = 7/8

Option 3: 4/8 + 2/8 = 6/8

Option 4: 6/8 + 2/8 = 8/8

**∴ The correct answer is 1/2 + 3/8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Target sum = 7/8

**Formula Used:** Sum of fractions = (Numerator₁ + Numerator₂) ÷ Common Denominator

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8f310d6a3e892edbf14bae9cfc4f6e2545c8eaf73009499dedd2c769313e73e5.png] 

Checking Option (2): 1/2 + 3/8

⇒ To add unlike fractions, find the LCM of denominators (2 and 8).

⇒ LCM(2, 8) = 8

⇒ Convert 1/2 to an equivalent fraction with denominator 8: (1 × 4) ÷ (2 × 4) = 4/8

⇒ Now, add the like fractions: 4/8 + 3/8

⇒ Sum = (4 + 3) ÷ 8 = 7/8

**∴ The correct answer is 1/2 + 3/8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Like and Unlike Fractions

Fractions with the same denominator are "Like Fractions" (e.g., 3/8, 5/8). Fractions with different denominators are "Unlike Fractions" (e.g., 1/2, 3/8).

Equivalent Fractions

Fractions that represent the same value even though they look different, found by multiplying/dividing numerator and denominator by the same number: a/b = (a × n)/(b × n).

LCM Method for Addition

To add unlike fractions, find the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the denominators to convert them into like fractions before adding.

questions.question: The difference of squares of two consecutive odd numbers is 64. What is the smaller of the two numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For consecutive odd or even numbers, the difference of their squares is always 4 × (the middle number).

Middle Number = 64 ÷ 4 = 16

The numbers surrounding 16 are 15 and 17.

Smaller Number = 15

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Difference of squares of two consecutive odd numbers = 64

**Formula Used:**

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8dce3c1d01bb6e708dc6a65331482c150bfe48f866b4723da9802959f47b6ca8.png] 

Let the two consecutive odd numbers be n and n + 2.

⇒ (n + 2)² − n² = 64

⇒ (n² + 4n + 4) − n² = 64

⇒ 4n + 4 = 64

⇒ 4n = 64 − 4

⇒ 4n = 60

⇒ n = 60 ÷ 4

⇒ n = 15

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference of Squares Property

For any two numbers a and b, a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b). If the numbers are consecutive odd/even, (a − b) is always 2.

Sum of First n Odd Numbers

The sum of the first n consecutive odd numbers is given by the formula n².

Arithmetic Mean of Consecutive Odd Numbers

The arithmetic mean (average) of two consecutive odd numbers x and x + 2 is the even number (x + 1) lying between them.

questions.question: frac{sqrt{8} + sqrt{50}}{sqrt{18}} = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Simplify each term by factoring out the largest perfect square.

√8 = 2√2, √50 = 5√2, and √18 = 3√2.

The expression becomes: (2√2 + 5√2) ÷ 3√2.

Summing the numerator: 7√2 ÷ 3√2 = 7/3.

**∴ The correct answer is 7/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given expression: (√8 + √50) ÷ √18

⇒ (√(4 × 2) + √(25 × 2)) ÷ √(9 × 2)

⇒ (2√2 + 5√2) ÷ 3√2

⇒ (2 + 5) × √2 ÷ (3 × √2)

⇒ 7√2 ÷ 3√2

⇒ 7/3

**∴ The correct answer is 7/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simplifying Radicals

A surd √x can be simplified if x has a perfect square factor 'a²', such that √(a² × b) = a√b.

Addition of Like Surds

Surds can be added or subtracted only if they have the same radicand (the number inside the root): m√x + n√x = (m + n)√x.

Product Property of Radicals

For any non-negative numbers a and b, the square root of their product is equal to the product of their square roots: √(a × b) = √a × √b.

questions.question: If a = 4 + sqrt{7}, b = 4 - sqrt{7} , then what is the value of a² + b² ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For conjugate surd pairs of the form x + √y and x − √y, the sum of squares is 2(x² + y).

Here, x = 4 and y = 7.

a² + b² = 2 × (4² + 7) = 2 × (16 + 7) = 2 × 23 = 46.

**∴ The correct answer is 46.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: a = 4 + √7 and b = 4 − √7

Formula used: a² + b² = (a + b)² − 2ab

⇒ a + b = (4 + √7) + (4 − √7) = 4 + 4 = 8

⇒ ab = (4 + √7)(4 − √7)

⇒ ab = 4² − (√7)² = 16 − 7 = 9

⇒ a² + b² = (8)² − 2(9)

⇒ a² + b² = 64 − 18 = 46

**∴ The correct answer is 46.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Squares Identity

For any two numbers x and y, the sum of their squares is x² + y² = (x + y)² − 2xy or x² + y² = (x − y)² + 2xy.

Conjugate Surds Property

The product of two conjugate surds (x + √y) and (x − √y) is always a rational number given by x² − y.

Square of Binomial with Surds

The expression (x + √y)² expands to x² + y + 2x√y, and (x − √y)² expands to x² + y − 2x√y.

questions.question: Which of the following number is NOT divisible by 8?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Any number divisible by 8 must be an even number because 8 is even.

Check the last digit of each option: 2736 (6), 5237 (7), 4360 (0), 5536 (6).

Since 5237 is an odd number, it cannot be divided by 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 5237.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given Numbers: 2736, 5237, 4360, 5536

Rule: A number is divisible by 8 if its last three digits are divisible by 8.

⇒ For 2736: Last three digits are 736. 736 ÷ 8 = 92 (Divisible)

⇒ For 5237: Last three digits are 237. 237 ÷ 8 = 29.625 (Not Divisible)

⇒ For 4360: Last three digits are 360. 360 ÷ 8 = 45 (Divisible)

⇒ For 5536: Last three digits are 536. 536 ÷ 8 = 67 (Divisible)

⇒ Only 5237 fails the divisibility test for 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 5237.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 2ⁿ

A number is divisible by 2ⁿ if its last n digits are divisible by 2ⁿ (e.g., last 2 digits for 4, last 4 digits for 16).

Divisibility by 3 and 9

A number is divisible by 3 or 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3 or 9 respectively.

Divisibility by 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd places and even places is 0 or a multiple of 11.

questions.question: Which of the following number is neither divisible by 3 nor by 11?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Divisibility by 3: Sum of digits must be divisible by 3.

Divisibility by 11: (Sum of odd-position digits) − (Sum of even-position digits) = 0 or multiple of 11.

Checking 4567: Sum = 4 + 5 + 6 + 7 = 22 (Not divisible by 3).

Checking 11 rule for 4567: (4 + 6) − (5 + 7) = 10 − 12 = −2 (Not divisible by 11).

Remaining options 3234, 2871, and 3003 are all divisible by both 3 and 11.

**∴ The correct answer is 4567.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given Numbers: 3234, 2871, 4567, 3003

**Testing Divisibility for each option:**

1) 3234:

⇒ Sum of digits = 3 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 12 (12 ÷ 3 = 4, so divisible by 3)

⇒ 11 rule: (3 + 3) − (2 + 4) = 6 − 6 = 0 (Divisible by 11)

2) 2871:

⇒ Sum of digits = 2 + 8 + 7 + 1 = 18 (18 ÷ 3 = 6, so divisible by 3)

⇒ 11 rule: (2 + 7) − (8 + 1) = 9 − 9 = 0 (Divisible by 11)

3) 4567:

⇒ Sum of digits = 4 + 5 + 6 + 7 = 22 (Not divisible by 3)

⇒ 11 rule: (4 + 6) − (5 + 7) = 10 − 12 = −2 (Not divisible by 11)

4) 3003:

⇒ Sum of digits = 3 + 0 + 0 + 3 = 6 (Divisible by 3)

⇒ 11 rule: (3 + 0) − (0 + 3) = 0 (Divisible by 11)

**∴ The correct answer is 4567.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 9.

Divisibility by 4

A number is divisible by 4 if the last two digits of the number are divisible by 4.

Divisibility by 6

A number is divisible by 6 if it is divisible by both 2 (ends in even digit) and 3 (sum of digits is divisible by 3).

questions.question: Average of consecutive natural numbers from 20 to N is 44. What is the value of N ? (where N is a natural number)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average of any consecutive series = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2

Given: Average = 44, First term = 20, Last term = N

44 = (20 + N) ÷ 2

88 = 20 + N ⇒ N = 68

**∴ The correct answer is 68.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First natural number (a) = 20

Last natural number (l) = N

Average of the series = 44

**Formula:**

Average of an Arithmetic Progression = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ae5271530760d333954aceb20443ea76e71abea46f049cedf4ccb9422f460bdb.png] 

Consecutive natural numbers form an Arithmetic Progression with common difference 1.

⇒ Average = (20 + N) ÷ 2

⇒ 44 = (20 + N) ÷ 2

⇒ 44 × 2 = 20 + N

⇒ 88 = 20 + N

⇒ N = 88 − 20

Draw a parallel line through point E to AB and CD.

The angle x is the sum of the supplements of the given angles.

Upper part of x = 180° − 100° = 80°

Lower part of x = 180° − 140° = 40°

x = 80° + 40° = 120°

⇒ CD || EF ∴ ∠ECD + ∠CEF = 180° (Co-interior angles)

⇒ 140° + ∠CEF = 180° ⇒ ∠CEF = 40°

⇒ x = 80° + 40° = 120°

questions.solution:

Since PQ || BC, the corresponding angle ∠ABC = ∠APQ = 75°.

Also, the alternate interior angle ∠PCB = ∠CPQ = 45°.

In triangle PBC, the sum of all internal angles is 180°.

∠CPB = 180° − (∠ABC + ∠PCB) = 180° − (75° + 45°) = 60°.

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

**Formula Used:** Linear pair axiom (Angles on a straight line sum to 180°).

⇒ ∠APC = 75° + 45° = 120°

⇒ ∠APC + ∠CPB = 180° (Linear pair)

⇒ 120° + ∠CPB = 180°

⇒ ∠CPB = 180° − 120°

⇒ ∠CPB = 60°

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

questions.question: As per provisions of the Inter-State River Water Disputes (ISRWD) Act, 1956, the Tribunal shall consist of a Chairman and two other Members nominated by the _______.

options.text: Central Government after consultation with State Governments

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chief Justice of India**__.

__
 
• The **Inter-State River Water Disputes (ISRWD) Act, 1956** is a specialized legislation enacted by the **Parliament of India** under the provisions of **Article 262** of the **Indian Constitution** to resolve water-sharing conflicts.
 
• According to **Section 4(2)** of the Act, a **Tribunal** established for the adjudication of a water dispute must consist of a **Chairman** and **two other members**.
 
• The **Chief Justice of India (CJI)** is the sole authority empowered to nominate these three members. The nominees must be sitting **Judges of the Supreme Court** or a **High Court** at the time of their nomination.
 
• The **Central Government** is responsible for the formal constitution of the Tribunal via notification in the **Official Gazette**, but it does not have the power to select or nominate the judicial members itself.
 
• This mechanism ensures **Judicial Independence** and impartiality in the adjudication process, as the disputes involve sovereign claims of different **State Governments** over natural resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 262 of the Constitution:** This article provides that neither the **Supreme Court** nor any other court shall exercise jurisdiction in respect of any such dispute or complaint that is referred to a **Tribunal** under the **ISRWD Act**.
 
• **Finality of Awards:** The decision rendered by the **Tribunal**, once published in the **Official Gazette** by the **Central Government**, has the same force and effect as an order or decree of the **Supreme Court**.
 
• **Entities in Options:**
 
 
• **President of India:** While the **President** appoints judges to the **Supreme Court** and **High Courts** under **Article 124** and **Article 217**, the specific nomination for this **ad-hoc Tribunal** is statutory and assigned to the **CJI**.
 
• **Central Government:** Its role is limited to forming the opinion that a dispute cannot be settled through **negotiations** and subsequently notifying the establishment of the **Tribunal** under **Section 4(1)**.
 
• **Chief Ministers:** Represent the **State Governments** which are the **litigants** in the dispute; hence, they are excluded from the nomination process to prevent **bias** or **Conflict of Interest**.

questions.question: Which of the following approach of human development is associated with Amartya Sen?

__
 
• The **Capability Approach** is a theoretical framework for human development pioneered by the Nobel Laureate **Amartya Sen** during the **1980s**.
 
• It shifts the focus of development from **economic growth** and **income levels** to the actual **freedoms** and **opportunities** individuals have to lead the lives they value.
 
• According to **Amartya Sen**, development should be seen as the expansion of **human capabilities**, which refers to the various combinations of 'functionings' (beings and doings) that a person can achieve.
 
• This approach was instrumental in the creation of the **Human Development Index (HDI)**, as it provided the philosophical backbone for moving beyond **GDP** as a measure of progress.
 
• It emphasizes that poverty is not just a lack of **income** but a **capability deprivation**, such as the inability to be healthy, well-nourished, or educated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Basic Needs Approach**:

 
 
• Initially proposed by the **International Labour Organization (ILO)**.
 
• Focuses on providing six essential requirements: **health**, **education**, **food**, **water supply**, **sanitation**, and **housing**.
 
 
 
• **Welfare Approach**:
 
 
• Treats humans as passive **beneficiaries** of development rather than active participants.
 
• It advocates for high **government expenditure** on social sectors like **healthcare** and **education** to improve living standards.
 
 
 
• **Income Approach**:
 
 
• The most **traditional** and oldest approach to human development.
 
• It links the level of **development** directly to the level of **income**, assuming higher income allows for greater **freedom**.

__
 
• The **Decision change** signal is used by a cricket umpire to indicate that a previously made decision or signal is being **revoked** or **altered**. Hence, the description matches the signal for a decision change.
 
• The physical action for this signal involves the umpire **crossing their arms** across their chest, typically with each hand touching the **opposite shoulder**. This gesture clearly communicates to the players, scorers, and spectators that the previous call is void.
 
• Under **Law 2.12** of the **MCC Laws of Cricket**, an umpire may alter a decision provided that the alteration is made **promptly** after the initial decision.
 
• This signal has gained significant prominence with the introduction of the **Decision Review System (DRS)**. When the **Third Umpire** overturns an on-field call, the on-field umpire must perform this signal before indicating the **new decision**.
 
• It is a vital communication tool to ensure **scoring accuracy**, as it instructs the **official scorers** to negate the last recorded event and replace it with the corrected outcome.

• Signaled by **waving an arm** from side to side, finishing with the arm across the chest. This signifies that the ball reached the **boundary** after touching the ground.
 
 
 
• **Dead ball:**
 
 
• Executed by **crossing and uncrossing wrists** below the waist. This indicates the ball is no longer in play due to various reasons like a bowler aborting their run-up or the ball getting lodged in clothing.
 
 
 
• **Short run:**
 
 
• Signaled by the umpire **bending the arm upwards** and touching the **near shoulder** with the fingertips. This occurs when a batsman fails to ground their bat behind the **popping crease** while completing a run.
 
 
 
• **No Ball:**
 
 
• Indicated by extending one **arm horizontally**, usually when a bowler oversteps the crease or performs an illegal delivery.
 
 
 
• **Wide Ball:**
 
 
• Signaled by extending **both arms horizontally**, indicating the ball passed too far from the batsman to be hit.

questions.question: In Haripala's "Sangeeta Sudhakara", written in the ____ century A.D., the terms Carnatic and Hindustani are found for the first time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**14**__.

__
 
• **Haripala** (also known as **Haripaladeva**), a king belonging to the **Yadava dynasty** of **Devagiri**, is the celebrated author of the musical treatise **Sangeeta Sudhakara**.
 
• The work **Sangeeta Sudhakara** was composed in the **14th century A.D.** and serves as a vital historical document in the evolution of **Indian Classical Music**.
 
• This text is particularly renowned for being the first literary source to categorize Indian music into two distinct traditions: **Carnatic** (South Indian) and **Hindustani** (North Indian).
 
• The categorization reflects the socio-cultural shifts occurring during the **Medieval period**, where regional variations became prominent enough to be formally recognized in theoretical texts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Evolution of Musical Traditions**:

 
 
• Prior to the **13th and 14th centuries**, Indian music was largely a unified system based on ancient texts like the **Natyashastra** by **Bharata Muni** and **Sangeeta Ratnakara** by **Sarngadeva**.
 
• **Carnatic Music**: This system remained more conservative, preserving the ancient **Svara** and **Raga** structures primarily in the southern regions of **Karnataka**, **Tamil Nadu**, **Andhra Pradesh**, and **Kerala**.
 
• **Hindustani Music**: This system evolved in the **North** through the synthesis of indigenous traditions with **Persian** and **Arabic** musical influences introduced during the **Delhi Sultanate**.
 
• The distinction noted in **Sangeeta Sudhakara** highlights the transition from **Gandharva** music to the regionalized **Desi** forms that eventually solidified into the two major schools recognized today.
